proposals.claim: Construct high-rise (12-14cm) pleated front with side-adjuster tabs instead of belt loops to reduce waistband compression in hot humid climates
proposals.rationale: Side adjusters eliminate continuous waistband pressure, allowing perspiration evaporation at the torso; pleats at high rise create expansion capacity for abdominal comfort during humidity-induced fabric relaxation
constraints: Requires 2-3cm side adjuster webbing tape reinforcement
Pleats must be stitched to side seam only, not across full width
Linen shrinkage contingency of 3-5% affects waistband sizing
evidenceNeeded: Linen fabric weight specification (gsm)
Humidity exposure duration data
Wearer abdominal relaxation measurements pre/post wear

proposals.claim: Construct mid-rise (10-11cm) flat-front with reinforced belt loops using cross-grain linen binding to maximize dimensional stability in tropical environments
proposals.rationale: Mid-rise with flat front minimizes fabric bulk at waistband; cross-grain binding counters bias stretch in high-humidity conditions where linen's hygroscopic properties increase lateral expansion
constraints: Belt loops must be interfaced with 100% linen twill tape minimum 15mm width
Cross-grain binding adds 0.5mm to loop seam allowance
Requires bar-tack reinforcement at each loop base
evidenceNeeded: Linen count and weave structure data
Dimensional stability test results under 85%+ relative humidity
Thread tension calibration for reinforced loops

proposals.claim: Construct high-rise pleated front with traditional belt loops but reduce loop diameter to 18mm to minimize moisture absorption points while maintaining waistband security
proposals.rationale: Smaller loop diameter reduces fabric surface area exposed to humidity; pleats provide volume accommodation; traditional loops preserve aesthetic while micro-sizing limits sweat permeation
constraints: 18mm maximum loop width requires precise folder attachment
Pleat stitching must extend 8cm minimum down leg to maintain crease definition
May not accommodate belts wider than 35mm
evidenceNeeded: Belt loop moisture absorption comparison data at standard vs reduced diameters
Crease retention testing under humid conditions
Wearer feedback on belt retention during perspiration

proposals.claim: Construct mid-rise flat-front with side-adjuster mechanism using 3cm webbing tabs with button-hole adjustment for minimal waistband contact and maximum ventilation in high-humidity wear
proposals.rationale: Flat front eliminates pleat bulk; side adjusters with gaps enable air circulation; button-hole adjustment allows waistband loosening without complete removal, managing sweat-induced fabric expansion
constraints: Webbing tabs must have minimum 3cm spacing between button stations
Fly construction must not interface with adjuster mechanism
Button holes weaken fabric; require reinforcement patches on inside
evidenceNeeded: Airflow measurement data through adjuster gap zones
Button hole durability testing under repeated adjustment cycles
Fabric reinforcement patch adhesion stability post-laundering

proposals.claim: Construct high-rise flat-front with tapered leg (17cm hem opening) using gradual side-seam taper starting at knee to reduce fabric volume while maintaining thigh ease in humid climates
proposals.rationale: Gradual taper preserves thigh expansion space needed for sitting/movement in heat while tapering ankles reduces lower-leg moisture retention; flat front minimizes abdominal compression

Thigh ease minimum 5cm over body measurement to accommodate heat-swelling
Hem construction must allow for potential future width adjustment
evidenceNeeded: Thigh circumference measurements at seated and standing positions in hot conditions
Moisture absorption rate comparison for tapered vs straight legs
Gait analysis data showing movement restriction thresholds

proposals.claim: Construct mid-rise straight-leg (22cm hem opening) with one-sided pleat on each front using structured linen to maintain volume and crease definition throughout humid day wear
proposals.rationale: Straight leg with consistent width accommodates swelling without silhouette distortion; single-sided pleats (vs double) reduce fabric bulk; structured linen resists the drape collapse common in sagging humid conditions

Structured linen finish may reduce breathability; select open-weave constructions
Single pleat asymmetry requires visual balance testing
evidenceNeeded: Crease retention testing on single vs double pleats at 80%+ humidity

Visual symmetry assessment under various lighting conditions

proposals.claim: Construct Korean-wide silhouette (24-26cm hem opening, minimal taper) with flat front and side adjusters to maximize thigh/hip volume while managing excess fabric drape in humid conditions
proposals.rationale: Wide silhouette provides maximum ease for perspiration-induced body swelling; flat front reduces waistband torso contact; side adjusters prevent waistband slip common in draping over-sized garments when wet

Excess fabric volume increases drying time post-laundering
May require internal horizontal darts at hip to control excess waistband fabric

proposals.claim: Construct crop-length (72-75cm inseam) straight-leg with pleated front and reinforced cuff hem using 1cm double-fold allowance to enable rapid moisture evaporation from ankle zone

Reinforced cuff adds 0.3cm to hem bulk; may feel restrictive
Visual balance requires coordinated footwear proportions
